feature.where: From the entrance, turn left and follow the path along the fence. Wild Lime is part of the shade on your right as you look toward the gazebo by the pavilion. Snake Plants and Crotons grow beneath its canopy. A second Wild Lime grows at the back of the park in the Natives area, near the palms and the Plumeria. Wild Lime stays green through the year. Its tiny yellow-green flowers are easy to overlook; the leaves, hooked thorns and citrus scent are useful identification clues in any season.

The easier one to see is on the west side, the side nearest the nursery, leaning out over the water; the other is across the pond, near the entrance loop of the drive. A third stands at Cypress Pond. In spring 2026 a young fern was found beside that pond as well, possibly the first new one to come up here on its own. feature.where: Coming from the office, it is the first big tree you reach at the front of Cypress Pond, on the right of the crushed-shell path. To its left stand two Red Silk Cotton Trees. Their gray, spiny trunks look much like the Kapok's, but they grow in a completely different way: low, level tiers of branches, where the Kapok holds its crown high on a bare trunk. Look up to see the difference.
